name: needs-drain-visual
description: Visual check of the four fatigue drain tiers (#928 — fatigue is the sole gauge): idle (0.5/tick), traveling (1/tick, a claimed job or a rest destination not yet reached), working (2/tick), and resting (0/tick, holds steady). Deterministic replay (seed:42, no player-random choices) with exact expected fatigue deltas at each checkpoint.

expect.note: idle tier: nothing claimed, nothing pending -> employeeWorkState 'idle' -> NEED_DRAIN_RATES.fatigue.idle (0.5) x normal-morale multiplier (1.0) = -0.5 exactly.

steps.description: Left unmarked: no UI control drives this exact command and none should exist -- employees.ts's own `dispatch` case comment: "no console command currently creates one" -- a test hook by design, same class as `employee assign_skill`. Targets a point far enough away (150,150) that several ticks of pure travel happen before arrival, isolating the 'traveling' tier's own drain rate from the 'working' tier that follows it.

expect.note: the dispatched work claimed but not yet promoted -- the employee has not moved yet this tick

Transition tick: the needs-drain step reads employeeWorkState BEFORE this same tick's dispatch-claim step promotes pendingTaskDuration, so this one tick still bills at the idle rate (-0.5) even though the employee is claimed as of this tick's end. The very next tick onward is the first to read 'traveling'.

traveling tier, isolated: 8 ticks at exactly -1.0/tick (NEED_DRAIN_RATES.fatigue.traveling x normal-morale multiplier 1.0), before the crew's rising morale later shifts the multiplier. This is the #928 fix under test -- pre-fix, this same outbound walk to a claimed job billed at the WORKING rate (2/tick, i.e. -16 over these 8 ticks), not this traveling rate.

steps.description: fatigue reads 91 here -- 9 below the post-hire 100, all drained at idle/traveling rates so far; the driller has not started any WORK yet (still walking toward (150,150)).

expect.note: Over these 65 ticks the driller finishes travelling (traveling tier), arrives and completes the dispatched general_work task (working tier, the fastest drain), then goes idle again (idle tier) once the task completes -- fatigue falls from 91 to exactly 24.475, low enough to trip the proactive-queue routing (NEED_WARNING_THRESHOLDS.fatigue = 25) and start a claimed rest the very tick this batch ends (restTicksRemaining becomes non-null). Exact value pinned because this whole replay is deterministic (seed:42, no player-random choices).

steps.description: fatigue reads ~24.475 -- the proactive rest has just been claimed and the employee is walking to (or already resting at) a living_quarters.

expect.note: resting tier: fatigue holds exactly flat across these 10 ticks (NEED_DRAIN_RATES.fatigue.resting = 0) -- restTicksRemaining counts down from 16 to 6 while the gauge itself never moves, confirming the rest doesn't keep leaking the way the pre-#680 idle-rate misclassification did.
